channel.description: Independent watchmakers recently added to the IndependentWatchmaking.com catalogue.

item.title: Lehmann (Hardt (Black Forest), Germany)
item.description:
Lehmann — Hardt (Black Forest), Germany

Lehmann is a small German watch manufacture in the Black Forest, founded in 2011 by Markus Lehmann in Schramberg. Lehmann spent some 20 years in the watch industry, much of it in precision engineering, and runs the family precision-machinery company Lehmann Präzision, which he took over from its founder Rolf Lehmann in 1998 and which builds turning and milling machines for the watch and optics industries. The watch manufacture is a division of that privately owned company. In early 2019 it moved from its first home at Gut Berneck in Schramberg to new premises in Hardt, at the Lehmann Präzision headquarters. Handelsblatt reported roughly 200 watches made in 2017, with a plan to reach about 500 a year from 2019 and around 18 people working in the manufacture; Lehmann does not publish current output.

View the full listing

item.title: Lang 1943 (Germany (watches assembled in Switzerland))
item.description:
Lang 1943 — Germany (watches assembled in Switzerland)

Lang 1943 is a watch brand named for Gerd-Rüdiger Lang, born in 1943 in Braunschweig, Germany, the watchmaker who founded Chronoswiss. Lang joined Heuer in 1964 in stopwatch production, moved to its Frankfurt branch in 1968 and to Munich in 1974, where he directed the technical department of Heuer Time GmbH. After Heuer closed the Munich subsidiary in 1980 he opened his own restoration and service atelier, and in 1983 he registered Chronoswiss, which he led until selling it in 2012. The new brand was conceived with German entrepreneur Georg Bartkowiak, a former CEO of Grieb & Benzinger, and was announced in the summer of 2022, with Lang acting as figurehead and adviser on design and technology. WatchTime and A Blog to Watch report that Lang died in 2023, and Bartkowiak now leads the brand. The articles used for this listing do not give a headquarters; Europa Star says the watches are assembled in Switzerland, and the official website, lang1943.com, was not yet working when this listing was written.

View the full listing

item.title: Juha Eskola (Helsinki, Finland)
item.description:
Juha Eskola — Helsinki, Finland

Juha Eskola is a Finnish independent watchmaker, born in Ostrobothnia, who works alone in his own workshop in Finland (Monochrome places him in Helsinki). He first studied marketing at the University of Turku, then applied to the Finnish School of Watchmaking in 2015 with the aim of becoming an independent watchmaker, graduating in 2018 ("independent watchmaking, or nothing", as he told Monochrome). He started with hand tools and prototypes and debuted in 2021 with his first handmade watch, the N1. Every watch carries his name on the dial and, by his account, takes well over 100 hours to make. No founding year is stated.

View the full listing

item.title: Hidaka Shinichi (Arakawa-ku, Tokyo, Japan)
item.description:
Hidaka Shinichi — Arakawa-ku, Tokyo, Japan

Hidaka Shinichi (Shinichi Hidaka) is a young, self-taught Japanese watchmaker who works as essentially a one-person operation under the name shinichi watch from a studio in Arakawa-ku, Tokyo. He describes himself with a joke, as "a comedian trying to make a watch", and the brand calls itself a "no-joke" label that does not take itself too seriously. By his own account he was once more interested in video games than in work, grew interested in design, and was then introduced to mechanical watches by a friend. He collected catalogues from local watch shops, studied makers such as Philippe Dufour, Masahiro Kikuno and Hajime Asaoka, learned how movements work through online research, taught himself CAD, and took odd jobs to pay for tools before starting to produce watches under his own name. No founding year is stated. Each model is treated as its own concept and project, with unusual dial designs drawn from vintage watches and Japanese anime and art, combining sourced parts with handmade elements such as dials and hands. The Kanji Dial Senju, priced at about US$1,500, carries kanji numerals, and the Mikawashima Super Pink Salmon Kanji dial, a 37mm 316L steel watch with solid caseback, ETA 7001 and Tatami-pattern strap, is a renewed colour of what he calls his favourite kanji dial. The Izanagi (also listed as 01) is a 37mm, 8.4mm-thick steel watch on the ETA 7001 with an aventurine dial, and the Shimadzu Dial Silver is a 41mm manual-winding watch on a three-quarter-plate Unitas 6498 with hand-blued steel leaf hands. A 40.5mm sector-dial watch, Perpetual Breeze, was made in collaboration with the Taiwanese brand BardsWhisper, with a handmade case and dial and a Sellita SW200 with a special rotor. Watches are sold as small made-to-order runs through the brand's online shop, with lead times of several months, and no cancellations or refunds on made-to-order pieces; most current listings are sold out. Prices on the brand's own site run from US$1,600 to US$2,200, and Grenon's of Newport, his only US retailer, lists his watches from US$1,700 to US$2,400. No production figures are published.

View the full listing

item.title: Alexey Yakushik Watches (Russia)
item.description:
Alexey Yakushik Watches — Russia

Alexey Yakushik Watches is an independent Russian watch brand founded in 2025 by Alexey Sergeyevich Yakushik, a designer who describes himself as an award winner in international competitions and the author of numerous publications. After a career in design he decided in 2025 to release his first watch collection, and the brand operates as his sole proprietorship, selling direct from its website with delivery by the Russian courier CDEK and through AllTime stores. The site gives no city or workshop address. The brand's approach is to build limited, numbered series around themes from Russian and Soviet popular memory — space exploration, war-time cinema and rock music — using established Swiss, Japanese and Soviet-era movements in cases designed by Yakushik rather than developing its own calibres. The first collection, Yuri Gagarin – First in Space, is a limited series of 130 pieces (65 in steel and 65 in black PVD) priced at 350,000 rubles, and the brand states that it holds the official right to use Gagarin's name and his "Poekhali!" phrase. It has a 45mm grade 5 titanium case and bracelet, a domed sapphire crystal, 100m of water resistance, BGW9 lume and a sapphire case back, and runs the AYW001.1, a movement based on the Miyota 8215 automatic with a custom rotor. Soyuz–Apollo marks the 50th anniversary of the 1975 docking of the two spacecraft in a series of 100 pieces, 50 in steel and 50 in black, on the Sellita SW200-1 in a 45mm steel case: the steel version carries an Earth element made of mokume-gane, a layered metal imitating Damascus steel, in titanium and gold, while each black version has an inlay of Muonionalusta meteorite, so no two dials are alike. It was launched at the Cosmonautics Museum in Moscow. "In Battle Go Only Old Men" is an 80-piece series marking the 80th anniversary of Victory, priced at 280,000 rubles and inspired by the 1970s Soviet film about a squadron of fighter pilots, with a black textured dial showing the Maestro aircraft and a five-pointed star. It uses the Soviet-designed Vostok 2409A in a 40mm steel case on an aged leather strap. The most affordable watch, Chaif – In the Rhythm of Rock, celebrates the 40th anniversary of the Yekaterinburg rock band Chaif with a bright orange dial, vertical markers evoking staff lines and hands shaped like a kefir bottle and half a loaf of bread, a reference to one of the band's songs. It has a 37.6mm steel case, sapphire crystal and the hand-wound Luch 1801.1N from the Minsk Watch Factory, and sells for 40,000 rubles, or 150,000 rubles in a gift set signed by the band, in a series the brand states as 100 pieces; the AllTime retailer lists it as 400 and as an entry in the Best Russian Watches 2025 contest's Independent Watchmakers category. Prices across the four series run from 40,000 to 350,000 rubles, and the total of the announced series is about 410 pieces. Gagarin watches are listed with a lead time of three to four months, and the brand ships within Russia.

View the full listing

item.title: echo/neutra (Piove di Sacco (Veneto) / Milan, Italy)
item.description:
echo/neutra — Piove di Sacco (Veneto) / Milan, Italy

echo/neutra is an Italian mechanical watch brand founded in 2018 by designer Nicola Callegaro and aerospace engineer Cristiano Quaglia, operating through the company ENCQ Srl. Callegaro founded the communication agency Zeppelin Studio in 2008, and Quaglia's background is in propulsion systems and sustainable innovation. Reports place the company in Piove di Sacco in the Veneto, with a dedicated Studio Milano as its first exclusive space, and the watches are described as Swiss Made and designed in Italy. The name nods to the architect Richard Neutra, whose houses were designed to be ready for anything, and the brand's collections take their names and inspiration from the Dolomites. Its stated philosophy is timeless design and durability, an emotional connection to the object, and a rejection of throwaway culture, with a deliberately distinctive rather than broadly appealing style. The debut Averau collection, launched on Kickstarter in 2018, is now a family of Swiss Made automatic field and tool watches on the Sellita SW279 elaboré. The 39mm Averau 39 comes in three-hand and moon phase versions, with Black, White (full lume) and Green and Blue Degradè dials from €690, and a double moon phase indicator from €890. The larger 42mm Averau Ceramic has a matte black ceramic case with a Grade 2 titanium TiFrame structure, in three-hand form at €970 and as a chronograph on the Sellita SW510 at €1,970. The 1956 collection is the vintage-inspired line, drawing on watches of the 1950s and 1960s and a contemporary field watch: 3H models from €840, GMT models on the Sellita SW330 from €1,290, hand-wound Sellita SW510M chronographs such as the Cortina-inspired bi-compax from €1,690, and tri-compax Chrono GMT watches with a second time zone and day/night indicator from €1,970. Cristallo is the brand's 42mm professional diver, named after another Dolomite peak, with a screw-down crown and 500m of water resistance on the Sellita SW279, from €1,190. Rivanera is a rectangular dress watch in sandblasted titanium described as shaped by advanced engineering and strict minimalism, at €1,490, with a smaller Piccolo version in a deep black finish with guilloché dials at €1,640, a Studio Edition sold only at Studio Milano and a Worn & Wound limited edition with Art Deco styling that has sold out. Under the One of a Kind banner, echo/neutra also makes single unique pieces that emerge from the design process and are never repeated, such as the Rivanera "Payne's Grey" (Archive 01), a Grade 5 titanium case on a manual-winding ETA 7001 with a Payne's Grey dial and copper-tone applied indices, and the matte black ceramic Averau Ceramic Chrono "Amaranth" (Archive 02), both of which have sold. echo/neutra also publishes an editorial series called Proud to Be Italian, which profiles Italian people and companies, beginning with the Sicilian agricultural estate Planeta. Prices across the range run from €690 to €1,970, the watches are sold direct with a two-year international warranty and free worldwide shipping, and some models are offered as pre-orders or sold out. No production figures are published.

View the full listing

item.title: L. Leroy (Bienne / Geneva, Switzerland)
item.description:
L. Leroy — Bienne / Geneva, Switzerland

L. Leroy is a revival of one of the great names of French and Swiss watchmaking. The house was founded in Paris in 1785 by Charles Leroy, the son of a watchmaker, and was soon appointed watchmaker to the king and later a supplier to the French imperial family. In 1835 it became watchmaker to the French Ministry of the Navy, supplying marine chronometers to the major European fleets until the late 1980s, and its clients over two centuries included Marie Antoinette, Queen Victoria, Napoleon III, Chopin, Louis Pasteur, Henri Matisse, Antoine de Saint-Exupéry and General de Gaulle. Its best-known creation, the Leroy 01 "La Lucie", was commissioned by the Lisbon collector António Augusto de Carvalho Monteiro and took seven years to develop: a gold pocket watch of 975 components and 27 complications that won first prize at the 1900 Paris Exposition Universelle and remained the world's most complicated watch until Patek Philippe's Calibre 89 in 1989. Louis Leroy also installed the first radio-telegraph time-signal system at the top of the Eiffel Tower in 1910, and the house sold an automatic-winding wristwatch as early as 1922.

View the full listing

item.title: Jacob & Co. (New York / Geneva)
item.description:
Jacob & Co. — New York / Geneva

Jacob & Co. is a New York jewellery and watch house founded in 1986 by Jacob Arabo, who remains its founder and chairman. Arabo arrived in the United States from the former USSR as a child with his parents and four sisters, spent his first American summer apprenticed to a watchmaker, then trained in jewellery and began designing and making pieces in his bedroom after hours before opening a booth in New York's Diamond District. The company's first watch came from a childhood memory of a two-timezone watch his father gave him: the quartz Five Timezone, made with simple bezels and straps because Swiss suppliers had turned him away. A photograph of Naomi Campbell wearing it put the brand on the map for watches, and when Arabo returned to Switzerland he worked with a boutique watchmaking firm on the Quenttin, a vertical tourbillon with a 31-day power reserve, retailing from US$360,000. Today the company combines a New York base with Swiss watchmaking, with boutiques in New York and Geneva, among other cities.

View the full listing

item.title: ZBL ZBIOLAND (Hong Kong)
item.description:
ZBL ZBIOLAND — Hong Kong

ZBIOLAND, shortened to ZBL, is a Hong Kong-registered brand founded in 2021 by Lu Jinzhi, who has spent more than 20 years in the watch industry and whose early skill at painting and love of science fiction led him to design his first wristwatch. The name reads as Z for 'zero origin,' BIO for life and vitality, and LAND for a creative territory free from the limits of traditional horology, and the stated aim is to give every watch a heartbeat and a vivid soul, drawing on interstellar machinery, urban architecture, and pioneering engineering. Its watches carry ZBL model numbers and run on a mix of Sellita SW200, Miyota, and modified 'ZBL in-house + SW' movements, plus the Barcelona's proprietary caliber.

View the full listing

item.title: Ollech & Wajs (Zurich / Haute-Sorne, Switzerland)
item.description:
Ollech & Wajs — Zurich / Haute-Sorne, Switzerland

Ollech & Wajs was founded in 1956 in Zurich by Joseph Ollech and Albert Wajs, who took a small shop at 55 Stockerstrasse with a retail counter just one metre long, selling Omega and Breitling. They began making their own watches in 1957, first as OWZ (Ollech & Wajs Zürich) and under the Helsa and Piz Palu names, settling on OW from 1959, the year Ollech designed the propeller-shaped OW mark. In 1958 they had become the first Swiss watch brand to sell by mail order, and in 1964 the Caribbean 1000 Precision shocked the industry with a certified 1,000-metre depth rating in a monobloc 'Triple-Safe' case, said to go 700 metres deeper than anything Rolex or Omega had achieved.

View the full listing

item.title: Nomadic Watches (Belfast, Northern Ireland, UK)
item.description:
Nomadic Watches — Belfast, Northern Ireland, UK

Nomadic was founded in 2021 in Belfast by Peter McAuley, a former mechanical engineer who sketched his first watches in a spare room, and takes its name from the SS Nomadic, the Titanic's tender. Its stated mission is to put Belfast on the watchmaking map in the way the city's shipbuilders once put it on the industrial one. Every watch uses a Swiss movement and is built in the flagship store by three Belfast-born watchmakers who handle assembly, regulation, and finishing, behind a glass wall visitors can watch through. Recurring signatures include engraved casebacks, a custom rotor, and a bright yellow seconds or GMT hand that nods to the Harland & Wolff shipyard cranes. Nomadic is the official timing partner of the United Rugby Championship and the North West 200, and backs every watch with a lifetime guarantee conditional on a service every five years, 30-day free returns, and free shipping.

View the full listing

item.title: Metrical Watch (Hong Kong)
item.description:
Metrical Watch — Hong Kong

Metrical Watch is an independent Hong Kong watch brand founded by Paul MH Li, operating as Metrical Watch Limited. Li came to watchmaking through a personal fascination with horology: hands-on study led him to design his own watches, and the first Metrical timepiece began as a sketch. The brand's stated approach is "Heritage Meets Innovation" — drawing on 18th- and 19th-century pocket watches while pursuing original design — and its Latin motto, "Symphonia Temporis Pulsans," reflects that classical grounding. Design and direction are done in Hong Kong, with Swiss movements and Swiss Made production, which Li describes as a commitment to quality and reliability.

View the full listing

item.title: Horologically Unique (Singapore)
item.description:
Horologically Unique — Singapore

Horologically Unique is the project of a single Singapore-based collector, who signs his notes only as 'A.' and describes himself as a guy who started a second Instagram page to sell part of his collection. That account, @horologically_unique, grew into a community, and he turned from selling vintage watches to making his own. He is explicit that the HU projects are not a brand or a business, there is no PR team, and the aim is accessible watches at the best quality he can manage. His brief for the first one was a clean, time-only dress watch that is affordable, thin, comfortable, and well made, with no logo on the dial, so the buyer pays for the watch rather than the label.

View the full listing

item.title: Epos (Lengnau, Switzerland)
item.description:
Epos — Lengnau, Switzerland

Epos traces its roots to 1925, when James Aubert founded James Aubert SA in the Vallée de Joux and devoted himself to chronographs and minute repeaters, handing his knowledge to his son-in-law Jean Fillon, who became Epos's leading watchmaker and the source of in-house complications such as a jumping hour and a regulator modification. The brand itself dates to 1983, when Peter Hofer and his wife Erna founded Montres EPOS SA at the height of the quartz crisis, betting on mechanical watches and working closely with Fillon for twenty years. In 2002 the Chonge-Forster family took over, with Ursula Forster, from a Swiss watchmaking family, as president and her husband Tamdi, a longtime Swiss watch industry executive, as CEO, broadening the range and expanding internationally under the slogan Artistry in Watchmaking.

View the full listing

item.title: CN Orologi (Milan, Italy)
item.description:
CN Orologi — Milan, Italy

CN Orologi, the watch house of CN Milano Srl, is the creation of Chiara Nardo, founder and creative director, who has designed the Italiano in Milan since 2020. Nardo says she grew up moving from one Italian city to another and cannot name a single place she belongs to; what shaped her instead was a shared culture of living, observing, and designing, and Italiano is the name she gave that identity. She describes her work as a balance of opposites — classic and contemporary, rigorous and natural, understated and sophisticated — aimed at making an identity visible rather than amazing the viewer. The design, the CN brand, and the Italiano logotype are registered with EUIPO and WIPO, and the brand says every part was designed and made exclusively for this watch.

View the full listing

item.title: Benrus (New York, USA)
item.description:
Benrus — New York, USA

Benrus was founded in New York in 1921 by Benjamin Lazrus and his two brothers, and the name joins the first syllable of his first name to the last syllable of the family name. The three pooled $5,000 to import Swiss movements and case them in the city, from the Hippodrome building in the jewellery district, which is still the company's address. A Charles Lindbergh campaign followed in 1926, and the 1929 Airman, with its cut-corner case and eagle-head corners in black enamel, was billed as the official watch of National Air Transport, later United Airlines. The 1940s Sky Chief, the brand's first chronograph, was sold as the 'Official Watch of Famous Airlines'.

View the full listing

item.title: Atelier Nossedh Chronometrie (Sweden)
item.description:
Atelier Nossedh Chronometrie — Sweden

Atelier Nossedh is a Swedish independent watch workshop founded by designer Alexander Gimell. The name Nossedh means "passing time" in Sámi. Gimell set out to make the small, classically proportioned, affordable chronograph he could not find for himself, and the brand describes itself as a workshop for experimentation and refinement rather than a conventional label. Scandinavian design is a stated influence: he starts with the case, aims for a classic-meets-modern look, and says every part of the design has a purpose, with nothing decorative that does not function. The company is registered as Atelier Nossedh AB; watches are Swiss made in small quantities, and no founding year or workshop address is published. The debut model, the AN.01 Chronograph, is a vintage-inspired hand-wound chronograph that draws on 1940s designs. Its 316L stainless steel case measures 37mm in diameter, 44mm lug-to-lug and 10.5mm thick (12.5mm with the double-domed sapphire crystal), with 19mm lug width and 50m water resistance. Linear brushing meets polished transitions, and concave curves on the bezel and caseback save material and improve comfort on the wrist. The bi-compax dial has a 30-minute counter at 3 o'clock and small seconds at 9, with applied indices, bevelled leaf hands and a tachymeter scale, and the buyer chooses Roman or Arabic numerals at checkout. Inside is the Sellita SW510 M in élaboré grade: manual-winding, 28,800 vph, 63 hours of power reserve, with a 30-minute chronograph counter, central chronograph seconds, small seconds and hacking seconds, regulated to about ±5 seconds per day. The AN.01 is offered in six colourways — sunburst black, blue and brown, and electroplated silvery-white, salmon and gold — on 19mm French Epsom leather straps with a polished steel pin buckle, and further strap colours are sold separately. Priced at €2,200, it was sold through pre-orders direct from the brand between 21 November 2025 and 30 January 2026, and the brand reviews it in Monochrome and Time+Tide describe it as a compact, accessible chronograph. No edition size is published; sales are in limited batches, and several colourways are currently listed out of stock.

View the full listing

item.title: Armand Nicolet (Tramelan, Switzerland)
item.description:
Armand Nicolet — Tramelan, Switzerland

The Armand Nicolet story begins around 1875 in Tramelan, in the Bernese Jura, where Armand Nicolet, the son of a watchmaker, set up his own Atelier d'Horlogerie after a brilliant apprenticeship. In 1902 he produced a pocket watch with a guilloché rose-gold case, an enamel dial, a single-button chronograph, a complete calendar, and an hour, quarter, and minute repeater, and his watches are still kept in the company museum. When he died in 1939 his son Willy took over and built the firm into one of the region's most important production facilities, and in 1987 Willy's chance meeting with the Italian watch entrepreneur Rolando Braga began a cooperation between Swiss technical skill and Italian creativity.

View the full listing

item.title: Arcturus (Singapore)
item.description:
Arcturus — Singapore

Arcturus is a Singapore microbrand founded in 2017 by Alexander Ian Loh, a legal counsel with a French multinational by day and, by night, a watch designer and watchmaker. It is named for the brightest star in the northern celestial hemisphere, reflecting the team's hope of becoming a supernova among microbrands and putting Singapore on the horological map. The four-person team also includes Ronald Chiam on finance and treasury, Sattish Segaran, a mechanical engineer who serves as Chief Artistic Officer, and Vin Chng on operations and logistics. Its Arcturus Promise is that no timepiece will go uncared for: every watch is tested and regulated before shipping, and LC-2 buyers receive a two-year international guarantee followed by Arcturus covering 50% of maintenance and repair costs for a further ten years.

View the full listing

item.title: Aera (United Kingdom / Switzerland)
item.description:
Aera — United Kingdom / Switzerland

Aera began in Geneva in early January 2018, when a small group of watch professionals from different corners of the industry met to answer one question: what defines a good watch? Their answer was that it should be honest, well made, and reasonably priced, and they took their cue from the tool watches of the 1950s and 1960s, not as retro copies but as contemporary, original designs. The name comes from the Latin 'era', a period of time with a distinct character. The brand sells under the line 'Swiss made, British design' and trades as Lone and Tonto Ltd in the UK. It launched with two models, the D-1 Diver and P-1 Pilot, and has since added the M-1 field watch and the C-1 chronograph.

View the full listing

item.title: Charles Berret (London, UK)
item.description:
Charles Berret — London, UK

Charles Berret is a London-born microbrand, designed in Britain around Swiss movements and launched in 2023 as what it calls an attempt to reinvent vintage horology with modern craft and technology. Its debut Darth Collection takes Gérald Genta's first design as its starting point, gives it a science-fiction aesthetic, and refines it with modern engineering; one reviewer called the result an affordable alternative to the Polerouter. The collection began as a limited run of 100 pieces presented as three interpretations: Asteria, Darth, and Arrow.

View the full listing

item.title: William Wood (United Kingdom)
item.description:
William Wood — United Kingdom

William Wood Watches was founded in 2017 by Jonny Garrett, named for his late grandfather, who served more than 25 years in the British Fire Service, stationed at Pilgrim Street with the Newcastle & Gateshead Fire Brigade on the Blue Watch shift. On 29 June 1966, William Wood and three colleagues saved five children, aged between one and five, from a house fire, earning the first Certificate of Merit ever awarded in the brigade's history; he passed away in 2009, before ever seeing the brand built in his name.

View the full listing

item.title: Raketa (Saint Petersburg, Russia)
item.description:
Raketa — Saint Petersburg, Russia

Raketa's roots run deeper than almost any watchmaker in this catalogue: the factory was founded in 1721 by Peter the Great as the Imperial Peterhof Factory, producing hardstone and lapidary works for the Russian court near St. Petersburg; a centre table it made for Emperor Nicholas I's 1844 gift to Queen Victoria still stands in Buckingham Palace today. After the Soviet revolution the factory turned to producing the Kremlin stars and Lenin's Tomb, then in 1938 began making the precision ruby stones used in watch movements — every Raketa watch since has carried 24 of them.

View the full listing

item.title: Laventure (Neuchâtel / La Chaux-de-Fonds, Switzerland)
item.description:
Laventure — Neuchâtel / La Chaux-de-Fonds, Switzerland

Founded in 2017 by Clément Gaud, Laventure remains, by the brand's own description, 'still a one-man show.' Gaud's passion for watches, chronometers, and instruments of measurement dates to childhood, shaped by growing up around antique shops; a design graduate, he spent five years at a Neuchâtel watch design agency working for major Swiss houses before going independent. The project began on Kickstarter with the original Marine collection, whose tonneau-shaped, lugless case and sandwich-construction dial with oversized lumed markers became the brand's signature, carried through nearly every release since.

View the full listing

item.title: Reverchon (Vallée de Joux, Switzerland)
item.description:
Reverchon — Vallée de Joux, Switzerland

Emilien Reverchon was born on 8 August 1988 in the Vallée de Joux, the son of a carpenter and a watchmaker; at ten, his grandfather, a micro-mechanic at Lémania, gave him his first watch, a moment he credits with cementing his passion. He joined workshops specialising in the decoration of grand complication movements early in his career, spending more than fifteen years working for some of the most prestigious houses in the Vallée de Joux before launching his own high-end watch decoration business. Since 2020 he has explored redesigning and transforming movement architectures himself, officially founding Reverchon as his own company in 2025.

View the full listing

item.title: Moriarty Watches (Ballyblood, Tulla, Co. Clare, Ireland)
item.description:
Moriarty Watches — Ballyblood, Tulla, Co. Clare, Ireland

Alison Moriarty is a Swiss-trained independent watchmaker and enamelist based in Ballyblood, Tulla, in Co. Clare, Ireland. A graduate of the Irish Swiss Institute of Horology, she became one of the youngest graduates of the prestigious WOSTEP Academy in Neuchâtel at just 21. She works alongside Mike Moriarty, who hand pad-prints every dial face on a custom-built Schmid machine, transferring ink to the fired enamel by feel without cracking it.

View the full listing

item.title: Jacques Etoile (Lörrach, Germany (now Pforzheim, under Aristo-Vollmer))
item.description:
Jacques Etoile — Lörrach, Germany (now Pforzheim, under Aristo-Vollmer)

Jacques Etoile was founded on 1 October 1996 in Lörrach, Baden-Württemberg, Germany, by master watchmaker Horst Jakob and his son Klaus Jakob, building on the reputation and component-industry relationships established by the family's own jewellery shop. The name is a French play on words: Klaus's Turkish wife was named Yıldız, Turkish for 'star' — 'étoile' in French — while 'Jakob' mapped loosely to 'Jacques.' Horst, who marked his own 50-year master-watchmaker anniversary in 2001, worked largely behind the scenes on technical development and models, while Klaus handled external relations, customer contacts, and trade fairs.

View the full listing

item.title: Vyntage Horology (Dubai, UAE)
item.description:
Vyntage Horology — Dubai, UAE

Vyntage Horology was founded by Mohammed Abdulmagied Seddiqi, part of the prominent Seddiqi family behind Ahmed Seddiqi & Sons, the UAE's leading distributor of Swiss watches for more than 70 years. The brand was created to give a platform to independent international designers, working out of Paris, who otherwise had no showcase for their work — pieces conceived as free creative expression rather than marketing-led design, watches meant to whisper their difference rather than announce it. Every watch is designed, constructed, and assembled in Switzerland in collaboration with independent designers and small workshops, then produced exclusively for the UAE market; production runs are deliberately small, with each design treated as a limited boutique edition rather than a mass-market release.

View the full listing

item.title: Roysdon Watch Co. (Texas, USA)
item.description:
Roysdon Watch Co. — Texas, USA

Dr. Paul F. Roysdon, Ph.D., came to watchmaking with no family workshop and no lineage to continue — a career spanning aerospace engineering, aerobatic flying, control systems and navigation, cybersecurity, machine learning, and national security leadership, having built and sold two aerospace and deep-tech companies along the way. He restored hundreds of vintage and modern watches, Breguet, Hamilton, Elgin, and Waltham among the historic pieces, Seiko, Patek Philippe, Rolex, Audemars Piguet, IWC, Longines, and ETA/Unitas among the modern ones, before deciding that taking a watch apart to understand it was no longer enough; he wanted to build one entirely himself.

View the full listing

item.title: Pragma (Geneva, Switzerland)
item.description:
Pragma — Geneva, Switzerland

Christopher Wegener discovered watchmaking at fourteen during a one-week internship, and spent the two decades that followed building a genuinely elite pedigree: an apprenticeship at Rolex, eight years alongside F.P. Journe contributing to the Chronomètre Souverain, the Octa, and the Chronomètre à Résonance, time at Laurent Ferrier working on natural escapement and tourbillon constructions, and years within a discreet, highly regarded manufacture building minute repeaters and tourbillons for houses that never put his own name on the result. Pragma, the brand he founded, frames itself explicitly as 'not a response to the market' but 'a response to a standard': every material sourced and documented, every component chosen twice — once for performance, once for provenance — with every supplier named publicly, down to the exact percentage of recycled content in each individual part.
